meta.title: Portolan: An opinionated standard for cloud-native geospatial catalogs
meta.description: Portolan publishes geospatial data as plain files on object storage, with no servers, no databases, and no proprietary licenses. Structured metadata lets a person or an agent read a catalog and query it directly. The standard sets the quality bar, a validator enforces it, tools make catalogs cheap to build, and a registry connects them into a network anyone can search.

hero.title: The future of spatial data
hero.description: Portolan is an opinionated standard for sharing geospatial data as cloud-native files on object storage, plus the tools that make it real. A Portolan catalog is a directory of open-format data described by structured <m>STAC</m> metadata, hosted on any S3-compatible bucket. No servers, no databases.

why.title: Spatial data infrastructure still assumes servers, databases, and specialists. Portolan doesn't.

open.title: Open and interoperable
open.description: Catalogs are built on established open formats like <m>GeoParquet</m>, <m>COG</m>, and <m>STAC</m> metadata. These work today in tools like DuckDB, BigQuery, Pandas, QGIS, and ArcGIS.

agents.title: Ready for people and agents
agents.description: A catalog describes itself in plain text and structured metadata. A person can read what the data is and where it came from. An agent can do the same, then query it directly with standard tools, no API or credentials needed. Because every catalog is described the same way, an agent can find a city's parcel data and a satellite archive, join them, and answer a question no single dataset could.

simple.title: Simple and scalable
simple.description: Running spatial data infrastructure normally means GeoServer or an Esri stack, with databases, services, and staff to keep them up. A Portolan catalog has none of that. Building one still takes work, which is what the CLI and validator are for, but once published it needs no maintenance, whether it holds megabytes or terabytes.

sovereign.title: Cheap and sovereign
sovereign.description: You choose where the data lives, including providers in your own country: AWS, Azure, GCS, MinIO, Hetzner, Scaleway, or any S3-compatible storage. You pay them for storage and bandwidth, and nothing else. No one sits between your organization and its data.

whoFor.title: Who it's for
whoFor.lead: Portolan was created for organizations that publish geospatial data and the people who use it.

large.title: Large publishers
large.today: Most people who could use a large geospatial archive never touch it because accessing the archive means creating an account, learning a custom portal, or installing a client library for its API.
large.change: With Portolan, publishers describe an archive once. Analysts and agents can then search and query the archive directly, including for uses the publisher never anticipated.

small.title: Small publishers
small.today: Cities have useful flood maps, building footprints, and other datasets sitting unpublished because sharing geospatial data has traditionally meant running a server and paying to maintain it.
small.change: A Portolan catalog is files in object storage. Nothing needs to keep running after publication, hosting can cost almost nothing, and the Portolan registry makes a city catalog discoverable alongside much larger archives.

users.title: Data users
users.today: Working with spatial data often means building a new pipeline for every source. A Portolan catalog tells users what a dataset covers and what its fields mean before they download anything.
users.change: Cloud-optimized formats let users fetch the two hundred megabytes they need instead of the forty gigabytes around them. Analysts can start working the day they find the data, while agents can query the same standardized metadata and files without a source-specific integration.

convert.title: Convert
convert.description: Any input becomes cloud-native, legacy formats or new ones alike. Vectors turn into <m>GeoParquet</m>, rasters into <m>COG</m>, tiles into <m>PMTiles</m>.

catalog.title: Catalog
catalog.description: A <m>STAC</m> catalog describes every asset, so any <m>STAC</m> tool can read it.

publish.title: Publish
publish.description: Push the files to any S3-compatible storage, from AWS, GCS, and Azure to R2, MinIO, or Source Cooperative.

browse.title: Use
browse.description: Use it with standard geospatial tools like DuckDB, Sedona, and QGIS, or point an agent at the URL.

cli.title: With the CLI
cli.description: Install <m>portolan-cli</m>, then <m>init</m>, <m>add</m>, <m>check</m>, and <m>push</m>. The CLI converts your files and generates the catalog.

claude.title: With Claude
claude.description: Install the Portolan skill in Claude Code and point it at your data. It handles conversion, metadata, and publishing. Agents excel at CLIs and text files, so non-experts can publish too.
